hook_text: Durban gets more than five times as much rain as Springbok. Why?
clip_script: Durban, KwaZulu-Natal: green hills, sugar cane, summer storms. Springbok, Northern Cape: rocky hills, low bushes, a dry riverbed. On a rainfall map, Durban is dark green: about 1,000 millimetres a year. Springbok is orange: less than 200. Rainfall decreases from east to west. The warm Indian Ocean brings moist air and rain to the east. The cold Benguela Current keeps the west dry. South Africa is a dry country. Save water.
visual_style: Whiteboard map of South Africa filling with colour from blue-green in the east to orange in the west, with arrows of moist air from the Indian Ocean.
mood: Clear and thoughtful, like solving a puzzle.
pacing: Compare two towns, then zoom out to the whole country.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find your own town on a rainfall map.
